<reason>A won by keeping the motion as class-wide digitization rather than a petition for one file, and by showing that only the government program can override a birth parent’s or nation’s “no.” B’s moral frame—wholesale harm, kinship as a network, the erased who cannot name a file—stayed live and made this competitive, but the concession that law-backed refusals block scanning sat in tension with category repair, and the attempt to collapse A’s locator into the same archive was answered. B’s clipped first rebuttal was a modest extra cost.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s non-compulsion answer (A4.2) with the class-versus-named-file distinction: a firm cannot legislate sealed files open, so “statute vs shareholders” is override power, not a better honor of consent.</best_rebuttal>
